criteria.title: Verifier is reliable, deterministic, and efficient
criteria.reason: tests/test_decisions.py is pure programmatic scoring against baked labels; no LLM judge, no network, no installs in tests/test.sh (pytest 9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf 0.5.2 are baked in tests/Dockerfile:8). Reference run: 10/10 tests in ~4 s; screen.py is byte-deterministic across two runs on batch A.

criteria.title: Solution demonstrates the task is solvable
criteria.reason: solution/solve.sh copies solution/screen.py to /app/screen.py and runs it; graded locally with the real verifier it scores A recall 0.9959 / precision 1.0, B recall 0.9992 / precision 0.9984, all 10 tests pass, batch runs take 2.3 s and 3.1 s against a 300 s budget.

criteria.title: Genuinely hard for good reasons
criteria.reason: Requires cross-script transliteration modelling (Arabic/Persian/Cyrillic/Chinese under ten-plus romanization conventions, 345 script-only entries), plus exact policy application (weak aliases, partial-date prefixes, identifier/date/lowest-uid tie-break) with seeded decoys; the reference engine is 880 lines and the floors (0.97/0.90 per class) leave little slack for heuristics.

criteria.title: Real-world value
criteria.reason: Sanctions screening engine acceptance testing against OFAC/HMT/EU-style lists is a paid compliance/vendor-validation job; task.toml relevant_experience and difficulty_explanation name the role.

criteria.title: Tests grade outcomes, not process
criteria.reason: Instruction states two deliverables and the CLI contract; the verifier only scores /app/decisions.csv and the output of running /app/screen.py on batch B (test_decisions.py:61-90, 93-115). Constraints (one file, stdlib, 300 s, one core) are mechanistic anti-cheat/portability constraints, not method prescriptions.

criteria.title: Tests resist adversarial agent behavior
criteria.reason: environment/Dockerfile copies only watchlist, customers, policy and dev/ (no labels for batch A); labels.csv, customers_b.csv, labels_b.csv live only in tests/ and are unlinked at import (test_decisions.py:37-43) before the engine runs as nobody with /tests and /logs/verifier chmod 700. Probed customers.csv: no extra columns, no invisible chars, customer_id order uncorrelated with class (2350 class transitions vs ~2345 random), only 36/3058 batch-A rows are answerable by exact dev lookup. Constant outputs fail (all NO_MATCH: recall 0; all MATCH: precision ~0.32). Hand-labelling batch A is defeated by batch B (5357 new customers, four conventions absent from A/dev).

criteria.title: No malicious code
criteria.reason: No network calls, no credential access, no obfuscation anywhere (grep for base64/eval/exec/socket/urllib across all files: none; zero-width/bidi scan: none). setpriv/prlimit in test_decisions.py:72-74 and chmod 700 in tests/Dockerfile:14 and test.sh:9 are legitimate hardening.

criteria.title: Tests verify behavior through execution
criteria.reason: Batch A is graded from the produced CSV; batch B executes the agent's engine end-to-end and grades its output. The only source inspection is the placeholder-sentinel check at test_decisions.py:63, which is a not-delivered guard, not a keyword test.

criteria.title: Consistent results, pinned deps, no live services
criteria.reason: Both images FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm; pip pins pytest==9.1.1 and pytest-json-ctrf==0.5.2; apt (util-linux) correctly unpinned; PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in both agent env and engine env; verifier.environment allow_internet=false. tests/generate_data.py regenerated all seven data files byte-identical to HEAD in 0.42 s (seeds 20260909 / 7 / 20260912).

criteria.title: Difficulty from reasoning, not formatting
criteria.reason: Output is a three-column CSV with two enum values; the verifier strips whitespace and tolerates extra trailing columns (test_decisions.py:51-57). All difficulty is in name equivalence and policy logic.

criteria.title: Tests and instruction describe the same behavior
criteria.reason: Every assertion maps to instruction.md or the in-environment /app/screening_policy.md Scoring section (0.97 recall/precision, 0.90 per class, 0.05 decoy, 0.01 unrelated, 0.97 uid accuracy, 300 s, one file, CLI flags). Caveat: the batch-B run also imposes prlimit --as 2 GiB, --fsize 50 MB, --nproc 64 (test_decisions.py:74) which the instruction does not state, though 2 GiB mirrors the environment memory_mb; and the per-class >=10-customer gate is only in task.toml (it only relaxes). Test file is 179 lines, above the ~100 guideline but readable.

criteria.title: Not solvable by memorization
criteria.reason: Fully synthetic 2100-entry list and 3058/5357-row batches from a custom rule-stacking romanization engine; no public solution exists and the policy's tie-break and weak-alias rules are task-specific.

criteria.title: Requires multi-step interaction
criteria.reason: The agent must read the policy, inspect the watchlist/customer schemas, build and iterate an engine against the labelled dev sample (/app/dev/) and produce two files; not a single-generation task.

criteria.title: Non-specialists can verify correctness
criteria.reason: Labels are derived by tests/generate_data.py (deterministic, single source of truth, verified byte-identical regeneration), not hand-coded; README class tables and the policy explain each class; spot check: all 8 no-DOB T11_twin labels obey the policy's lowest-uid rule.

criteria.title: Human-written, concise, absolute paths
criteria.reason: Three short paragraphs, absolute backticked paths, no headings, no tool lists, reads as a practitioner's brief ('I will run that file myself'). Minor: 'Read it first' is a small process nudge, and the third paragraph restates variation categories already in the policy.

criteria.title: Solution computes, not hardcodes
criteria.reason: solve.sh is 5 lines; the 880-line engine is a separate file (solution/screen.py) that reads only its three CLI inputs (lines 867-872), contains no uid literals, and computes every decision.

criteria.title: Verifier inputs sufficient, tooling baked
criteria.reason: artifacts = [/app/decisions.csv, /app/screen.py] are the only agent paths read; everything else is under /tests/data (COPY . /tests/). Verifier tooling baked in tests/Dockerfile; test.sh installs nothing. watchlist.json md5 749ffc77... identical in environment/data and tests/data.

criteria.title: Clean agent image; verifier owns deps; apt cleanup
criteria.reason: environment/Dockerfile copies only data files, installs nothing test-only; tests/Dockerfile does apt-get update && install util-linux && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* and excludes/removes generate_data.py (tests/.dockerignore, Dockerfile:14). All 22 tb3 static checks pass when run locally.

criteria.title: Exact schema documented
criteria.reason: instruction.md gives the exact header and value set; screening_policy.md 'Output' section restates it normatively and 'Inputs' documents the watchlist and customer schemas.

criteria.title: No typos in identifiers
criteria.reason: Paths, flags (--watchlist/--customers/--out) and filenames agree across instruction.md, solve.sh, test_decisions.py, Dockerfiles and README; instruction trailer matches CONTRIBUTING exactly with N=14400 = agent timeout.

criteria.title: Difficulty explanation quality
criteria.reason: Names the core difficulty (romanization systems, decoy classes, sample not covering conventions), states the data is synthetic and modelled on OFAC/HMT/EU practice, and names the real-world role; framed as task properties, not agent pass rates.

criteria.title: Solution explanation quality
criteria.reason: Describes the phonological skeleton/vowel-slot model, script handling, Chinese reading sets, lexicon and watchlist-learned equivalents, and the policy ordering; matches the functions actually present in screen.py (transliterate, readings, _slots_compatible, learn_script_equivalents, screen).

criteria.title: Verification explanation quality
criteria.reason: Describes both batches, the unprivileged run, label deletion, every threshold and the >=10 class gate, all consistent with test_decisions.py. Threshold calibration cites the reference (0.996/1.0 on A, 0.999/0.998 on B) and one independent agent implementation on A (0.994/0.999); no independent implementation is cited for batch B, so calibration of the B floors rests on the reference alone.

criteria.title: Category and tags
criteria.reason: category Operations / subcategory Compliance matches docs/TAXONOMY.md line 53; tags [compliance, entity-resolution, transliteration, python, data] are specific.

criteria.title: Task folder name
criteria.reason: 'sanctions-name-screening' is three kebab-case words and describes the task exactly.

criteria.title: Timeouts and resources
criteria.reason: verifier 600 s (engine budget 300 s, reference ~4 s total), agent 14400 s, 1 cpu / 2048 MB / 5120 MB deliberately set below template storage; difficulty is reasoning not compute. Note: agent timeout (4 h) is below the expert estimate (6 h).

criteria.title: README provides useful context
criteria.reason: Adds the variation-class tables, reproduction commands and file map not found elsewhere; the four explanation sections duplicate task.toml but CONTRIBUTING requires them. Nits: refers to 'the repository's scripts/score.sh' which is outside the task directory and will not exist in the terminal-bench tree; the class table omits R1_random_entity and R2_random_vessel, which the verifier does gate at 0.01.

criteria.title: Expert time estimate
criteria.reason: 6.0 h is set and plausible for an expert who knows the approach, though the 880-line reference suggests it is on the optimistic side.

criteria.title: Only valid fields
criteria.reason: Uses artifacts, [task] (name/description/authors, same shape as merged task atrx-vep-crispr), [metadata] with only the listed keys incl. relevant_experience, [verifier], [verifier.environment], [agent], [environment]; no invented fields; check-task-fields.sh passes.

criteria.title: No extraneous files
criteria.reason: Every file is a scaffold, Dockerfile-copied data, the solution, or the verifier; tests/generate_data.py is the label provenance (referenced by README, excluded from both images) and tests/.dockerignore is what excludes it. No editor/OS cruft (git ls-tree matches find).

criteria.title: Artifacts narrow, fail-safe collects
criteria.reason: Only two small agent-produced files are shipped; watchlist and batch B are baked into the verifier image rather than transferred; no [[verifier.collect]] hooks.

criteria.title: Agent code runs unprivileged; reward protected
criteria.reason: test.sh chmod 700 /logs/verifier before pytest; /tests is 700; the engine runs via setpriv --reuid=nobody --no-new-privs plus prlimit in a fresh session with output to files, the process group is SIGKILLed after, and root derives reward from pytest's exit code (test.sh:11-18). No agent module is imported into the pytest process. A setsid() grandchild could outlive killpg, but as nobody it cannot reach the reward channel.

criteria.title: CTRF report emitted
criteria.reason: test.sh:11 runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json; local run produced a 10-test CTRF summary.

criteria.title: Do-not-modify constraints enforced
criteria.reason: instruction.md contains no constraint protecting a concrete artifact from modification; the verifier uses its own pristine copies of watchlist and batch B regardless.

criteria.title: Reward is exactly 0 or 1
criteria.reason: test.sh:14-18 writes 1 on pytest exit 0 and 0 otherwise; no other path writes reward.txt.

top_risks: Open-internet reconstruction: tests/generate_data.py with hard-coded seeds (SEED_HIDDEN=20260909, SEED_B=20260912) and the literal labels_b.csv/customers_b.csv will be public in the merged repo; an agent that fetches them can regenerate both label files and a batch-B lookup table. This is the benchmark-wide exposure of any tests/ directory, mitigated only by the 'do not cheat' trailer, but here it also hands over the held-out batch, so it deserves an explicit note in the PR.

The held-out batch is not really blind: instruction.md and screening_policy.md enumerate batch B's four extra conventions with example spellings (Cemal, Huseyin, Ahmet, Kasim; Achmad, Joesoef, Sjarif; Cajkovskij, Zukov, Sevcenko; Tan, Lim, Ong, Goh, Teo), turning 'generalise to unseen conventions' into a checklist. Also screening_policy.md, an in-world bank policy, speaks of 'the verifier' and 'the task passes', which reads as benchmark language leaking into the environment.

Undocumented verifier limits on the batch-B run: RLIMIT_AS 2 GiB, fsize 50 MB, nproc 64 (test_decisions.py:74) are not in instruction.md, which only promises one core and 300 s. A legitimate engine that maps more virtual memory than RSS (threads, large dicts) would fail with an opaque error; state the limits or drop --as.

Reference solution is visibly fitted to the generator: token alternatives mirror the generator's rule list one-for-one (Turkish final t for d, Indonesian sj/oe/dj, scientific z/c/s) and 127 of 341 LEXICON spellings appear verbatim in generate_data.py. A reviewer may ask whether the 'rules' encode real transliteration knowledge or the author's inverse of their own generator, and whether a 6 h expert estimate (with a 4 h agent timeout) is consistent with an 880-line engine.

README/metadata polish: README points at a repo-external scripts/score.sh that will not ship; the class table omits R1_random_entity/R2_random_vessel which the verifier gates; the four explanation sections are verbatim copies of task.toml; and calibration of the batch-B floors cites only the reference implementation, not an independent one.
